title: Duplicate IDs in the Lane
description: Two cards in the same lane sharing one id/data-testid is exactly the kind of bug that makes a naive #id selector grab the wrong shipment — Practice mode can force it deliberately so you can practice scoping your locators correctly.
successCondition: With Practice mode's "Duplicate ids" toggle switched on and a lane containing at least two shipment cards, a test confirms a bare id/data-testid selector for that shared id now matches more than one element in that lane (proving the duplication is real), then successfully drags the SECOND of the two duplicate-id cards specifically — by scoping the locator to its parent lane container plus its distinguishing content (shipment id text or position) rather than the shared id alone — and confirms the correct shipment (not its neighbor) ends up moved.
hints: The toggle lives under "Locators" in the Practice mode drawer — with duplicateIds on, the second row in any lane with 2+ cards is deliberately given the first row's id.
A framework's getByTestId-style locator will throw or pick an arbitrary match when more than one element shares an id — scope to the lane column, then filter by visible text, to disambiguate.
